subject: Microeconomics: supply and demand equilibrium, elasticity, per-unit tax, consumer surplus

items.answer: The curves intersect at P = 20 and Q = 60 (equilibrium price $20, equilibrium quantity 60 units).
items.method: Find the crossing point of the demand and supply lines in the graph.
Set quantity demanded equal to quantity supplied and solve for P, then substitute back.
Evaluate both curves at the ceiling price; shortage = Qd - Qs.

items.answer: The ceiling of $15 is below the equilibrium price of $20, so the market price cannot rise to its equilibrium level and quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied.
items.method: A price ceiling binds only if it is set below the equilibrium price.
Point elasticity = slope of the demand function dQ/dP times P/Q at the equilibrium.

items.answer: Q falls from 60 to 50 and P rises from 20 to 25. %dQ = -10/55 = -18.18 %, %dP = 5/22.5 = 22.22 %, so E = -0.818 (absolute value 0.82).
items.method: Midpoint formula: change divided by the average of the old and new values for both Q and P.

items.answer: Demand is inelastic (|E| < 1), so a price increase raises total revenue: 20 x 60 = $1200 before and 25 x 50 = $1250 after.
items.method: Inelastic demand: the percentage fall in quantity is smaller than the percentage rise in price, so revenue P x Q rises.

items.answer: Sellers receive P_c - 6, so supply becomes Qs = -20 + 4 (P_c - 6) = -44 + 4 P_c. Setting 100 - 2 P_c = -44 + 4 P_c gives P_c = 24 and Q = 52. Consumers pay $24, sellers receive 24 - 6 = $18.
items.method: Shift the supply curve by the tax (producer price = consumer price - t), solve for the new equilibrium.

items.answer: Consumers pay 24 - 20 = $4 more per unit (2/3 of the tax), producers receive 20 - 18 = $2 less (1/3 of the tax); 4 + 2 = 6.
items.method: Compare the post-tax prices with the pre-tax equilibrium price of $20.

items.answer: Tax revenue = t x Q = 6 x 52 = $312
items.method: Tax per unit times the quantity traded after the tax.

items.answer: Deadweight loss = (1/2) x t x (Q_before - Q_after) = 0.5 x 6 x (60 - 52) = $24
items.method: Area of the triangle between the supply and demand curves for the lost units.
Triangle area under the demand curve above the price: half base times height, with choke price 50.

items.answer: After the tax P_c = 24 and Q = 52: CS = (1/2) x (50 - 24) x 52 = $676
items.method: Same triangle with the consumer price and quantity from Problem 3.
Difference of the two consumer surpluses; (tax revenue 312 + deadweight loss 24 = 336 = 224 + producer surplus loss 112).
